title: FTC Settles with Cox Media Group Over Deceptive 'Active Listening' AI Marketing Claims
description: FTC requires Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1 million to settle charges they deceived customers about 'Active Listening' AI-powered marketing service. The companies claimed their service listened to consumer conversations through smart devices, but the service did not actually listen in on conversations or use voice data. Instead, they resold email lists from other data brokers at a significant markup. FTC clarified that clicking through mandatory terms of service does not constitute 'opt-in consent' for invasive data collection.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette Agent: First Release of Extensible AI Assistant
description: Simon Willison announced the first release of Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette. This represents the integration of his LLM Python library (developed over 3 years) with Datasette, providing an extensible AI assistant with features like Fly Sprites sandbox for running commands, 'View SQL query' buttons for charts, improved handling of truncated responses, and better permission tracking.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic Signs $1.25B/Month Compute Deal with SpaceX
description: SpaceX S-1 filing reveals Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to compute capacity across COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May and June 2026 at reduced fees. Either party may terminate with 90 days notice.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google Gemini 3.5 Flash: More Expensive but Google Plans to Use It Everywhere
description: Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash at Google I/O, skipping the preview modifier and going straight to general availability. Google appears to be using it across many key products. Analysis includes discussion of Gemini Spark (Google's OpenClaw competitor), security concerns around prompt injection, enterprise-grade security with isolated VMs, and the transition from open source Gemini CLI to closed source Antigravity CLI.
author: Simon Willison

title: The Last Six Months in LLMs in Five Minutes
description: Simon Willison presented a five-minute lightning talk at PyCon US 2026 covering the latest developments in LLMs from the past six months. The presentation uses his annotated presentation tool and provides a comprehensive overview of recent LLM advancements.
author: Simon Willison

title: UK Government Digital Service Weighs in on NHS Open Source Decision
description: The Government Digital Service (GDS) published 'AI, open code and vulnerability risk in the public sector' on May 14th, responding to the NHS's decision to close down access to their open source repositories. Key recommendation: 'Keep open by default. Making everything private adds additional delivery and policy costs, and can reduce reuse and scrutiny. Openness should remain the default posture, with closure used sparingly and deliberately.' Terence Eden interprets this as a major escalation in civil service terms.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenClaw's Six Name Changes Since November
description: Analysis of OpenClaw's naming history through Git commits, showing six different names: Warelay → CLAWDIS → CLAWDBOT → Clawdbot → Moltbot → OpenClaw. The detailed timeline shows the evolution from 'WhatsApp Relay CLI' to 'Personal AI Assistant' between November 2025 and January 2026.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette LLM Limits: Per-User Spending Limits for LLM Usage
description: A new Datasette plugin that works with datasette-llm and datasette-llm-accountant to configure per-user or global spending limits for LLM usage inside Datasette. Configuration example shows rolling 24-hour window with $1.00 per user daily limit. Also includes updates about tool availability permissions and background agent tools.
author: Simon Willison

title: Hacker News Discussion: Runtime - Sandboxed Coding Agents for Teams
description: Launch HN: Runtime (YC P26) - Sandboxed coding agents for everyone on a team. The discussion covers 84 points with 22 comments, focusing on the approach of providing sandboxed AI coding assistants that can be used across entire teams rather than individual developers.
author: Hacker News

title: Google's Antigravity Bait and Switch
description: Hacker News discussion with 654 points and 298 comments about Google's transition from open source Gemini CLI (Apache 2.0 licensed TypeScript) to closed source Antigravity CLI. The discussion covers concerns about Google's changing stance on open source tools for AI development.
author: Hacker News

title: Multi-Stream LLMs: New Paper on Parallelizing Prompts, Thinking, I/O
description: Hacker News discussion (100 points, 12 comments) about a new arXiv paper on Multi-Stream LLMs that explores parallelizing and separating prompts, thinking, and input/output operations. This represents an architectural approach to improving LLM performance and efficiency.
author: Hacker News

title: Show HN: KVBoost – Chunk-level KV Cache Reuse for HuggingFace (5-48x Faster TTFT)
description: Release of KVBoost, a tool for chunk-level KV cache reuse for HuggingFace models, achieving 5-48x faster Time To First Token (TTFT). This is a significant performance optimization for transformer-based models, reducing latency in LLM inference.
author: Hacker News

title: CODA: Rewriting Transformer Blocks as GEMM-Epilogue Programs
description: arXiv paper discussed on Hacker News (49 points, 3 comments) about rewriting transformer blocks as GEMM-epilogue programs. This represents a systems-level optimization approach for transformer architectures.
author: Hacker News
